title: Wellmanifest Reuse Policy Standard
description: Rules and governing requirements for cross-project code discovery, deduplication, modular extraction, and documentation across user-authored repositories.

rules.name: Search Before Generate
rules.statement: Before generating a new utility module, CLI tool, or service component from scratch, the author or autonomous agent MUST query the local workspace index (via semcod/search / subactor-search) for existing implementations, models, and shared libraries.
rules.remediation: Query `subactor-search ask "<concept>"` and review candidate projects before scaffolding.

rules.name: Duplication & Clone Detection
rules.statement: Repositories MUST be analyzed for AST and block duplication using semcod/redup. Internal clone groups with >= 10 lines and >= 0.80 similarity must have an active refactoring plan or modularization ticket.
rules.remediation: Run `redup scan .` and decompose identified clones into planfile refactoring tasks.

rules.name: Continuous Modularization & Extraction
rules.statement: When identical or near-identical logic is identified across 2 or more repositories via `redup compare`, the logic MUST be considered for extraction into an independent package (under `packages/<name>` or a dedicated domain repo in wellmanifest/* or semcod/*) with pinned interfaces. Before treating cross-repository standard copies as refactoring debt, classify their relationship using wellmanifest.ssot/decision/v1 and bind each canonical source to a full Git revision. Reuse an existing HOME before creating a new standard. Generated mirrors and vendored copies are retained when exact source parity is verified; changed or unknown copies remain review findings. Shared command names alone do not prove shared semantics.
rules.remediation: Decompose into an extraction ticket: isolate function/class, write unit tests, export entry point. Use the shared standard/standard-sources.ssot.json profile and scripts/check_standard_sources.py with an explicitly supplied workspace and pinned SSOT schema root. Update the canonical owner, then distribute through the owning adoption mechanism; never edit a managed copy to hide drift.

rules.name: Structured Planfile Decomposition
rules.statement: Reuse and deduplication efforts MUST be broken down into structured, prioritized tickets in .planfile/sprints/current.yaml following the 5-phase lifecycle: DISCOVER -> COMPARE -> EXTRACT -> CONSUME -> VERIFY.

rules.name: Autonomous Execution Delegation (Koru Handoff)
rules.statement: All generated reuse and deduplication tickets intended for autonomous delivery MUST include `tier: refactor` or `tier: reuse`, labels `[koru-autonomous, reuse]`, deterministic verification commands, and exit code 0 acceptance criteria.
rules.remediation: Include koru handoff metadata in ticket definitions for autonomous processing via `koru --queue`.

rules.name: Enforced Documentation & Telemetry Standards
rules.statement: All non-fork, user-authored repositories MUST enforce wellmanifest/docs (Compact v2: max 120 lines / 600 words per doc, clear docs/ index) and wellmanifest/logs (errors/{CODE}.md runbooks, structured JSONL logs). Documentation auto-sync SHOULD leverage semcod/code2docs.
rules.remediation: Initialize docs/ with compact markdown specs and add error runbooks for all handled exit codes.

rules.name: Semantic AST & Logic Profiling
rules.statement: Code analysis before modularization or deduplication MUST generate structural AST and function logic profiles (via semcod/code2logic) to identify identical signatures, schemas, and control flows across modules.
rules.remediation: Run `python3 -m code2logic <target> -f toon --does` to extract AST function models and logic specifications before refactoring.

rules.name: Canonical Contract & DSL Generation
rules.statement: Extracted shared data structures, configurations, and API interfaces MUST have a canonical DSL schema (via autogrammar/code2schema and data2dsl) committed alongside the shared library to prevent schema divergence.
rules.remediation: Generate canonical JSON/DSL schemas using `code2schema` or `data2dsl` and validate with `diff-dsl`.

rules.name: Sequential Intent Ticket Dispatch
rules.statement: Multi-repository reuse and deduplication migrations MUST be decomposed into sequential intent tickets governed by subactor/intent (`intent.json` / `wellmanifest.intent/v3`) with explicit budgets, allowed paths, and lease fencing.
rules.remediation: Generate intent specifications using `scripts/generate_reuse_intent.py` and coordinate sequential delivery through Subactor or Koru.

rules.name: Behavior Parity & Verification
rules.statement: Every deduplication and shared library extraction MUST provide deterministic automated verification (via unit tests and autogrammar/testql scenarios) asserting 100% behavioral parity before and after extraction.
rules.remediation: Author TestQL verification scenarios or unit test suites exercising the shared contract against both the extracted source and the calling projects.

rules.name: Single-Exporter Thin Facade & Re-Export Delegation
rules.statement: When logic is shared across repositories or split out of a god module (>500 lines), exactly one canonical HOME module MUST own the implementation (per wellmanifest/modularity single-exporter), while consumer or compatibility modules MUST act as thin facades (<=150 lines) that import and re-export or adapt the canonical symbols rather than maintaining parallel copies of implementation functions.
rules.remediation: Extract shared logic to the canonical HOME module and replace duplicate consumer modules with thin re-export facades.

rules.name: Declarative Command, Operation & Route Registry
rules.statement: CLI subcommand parsers, HTTP route dispatchers, and operation catalogs with 5 or more branches MUST use a declarative specification table (CommandSpec / RouteSpec / OperationSpec registry) mapped to dedicated handler modules (*_commands.py, *_handlers.py, *_helpers.py) rather than imperative if/elif chains or inline parser boilerplate.
rules.remediation: Refactor imperative CLI/HTTP/operation dispatchers into a declarative spec table and move handlers into a dedicated *_commands.py or *_helpers.py module.

rules.name: Canonical Infrastructure Primitives (MtimeCache, SqliteBatchStore, GitRefReader)
rules.statement: Repositories MUST NOT re-implement ad-hoc uncached YAML/JSON/AST file parsing inside loops, unbatched SQLite .execute() loops, or repeated `git rev-parse` subprocess spawns; they MUST reuse canonical primitives: (path, mtime_ns, size)-keyed LRU caching, contextlib.closing() + batched SQLite transactions (executemany / WHERE IN), and pure-Python .git/HEAD ref readers.
rules.remediation: Replace ad-hoc loop I/O, unbatched SQLite queries, and git subprocesses with canonical mtime-cached loaders, batched SQLite helpers, and pure-Python Git ref readers.

rules.name: Vendored Mirror & Cross-Org Identity Parity Binding
rules.statement: Every vendored, overlay, or generated mirror directory (e.g., vendor/*, overlay/*, generated/parallel/contexts/*) MUST either be replaced by a thin import facade or registered in standard-sources.ssot.json (wellmanifest.ssot/decision/v1) with SHA-256 parity verification; hardcoded legacy organization slugs across governance, planfile, or package metadata are prohibited.
rules.remediation: Register necessary distribution mirrors in standard-sources.ssot.json with pinned SHA-256 digests or replace them with thin import facades, and align organization slugs with the repository remote.

rules.name: Horizontal Complexity & Peer Fan-Out Ceiling
rules.statement: Modules and functions MUST bound horizontal complexity: wide imperative if/elif chains (>= 5 branches), excessive same-layer peer import fan-out (> 12 imports), and monolithic orchestrator modules (> 500 lines) MUST be refactored into declarative decision tables, prioritized dependency resolvers, and vertical/stream pipelines.
rules.remediation: Run `python3 -m standard.stream_flow --project <repo_dir>` and refactor wide branching or fan-out hotspots into DecisionEngine and StreamPipeline stages.

rules.name: Declarative Decision Graph & Lexicographic Priority Routing
rules.statement: Multi-branch routing and policy decisions MUST be expressed as reusable DecisionRule specifications ordered by lexicographic priority tier (`floor` > `standard` > `opportunistic`, per wellmanifest/priority) and numeric weight, with explicit `when` and `satisfied_when` predicates and deterministic decision trace receipts.
rules.remediation: Replace imperative if/elif trees with a declarative DecisionEngine table (`standard.stream_flow.DecisionEngine`).

rules.name: Prioritized Dependency & Fallback Chain
rules.statement: Runtime and module dependencies with alternatives or degradation paths (e.g., native Rust extension -> pre-warmed UDS daemon -> cached projection -> Python stdlib fallback) MUST be declared as PrioritizedDependency nodes with readiness probes and deterministic fallback edges instead of scattered try/except imports.
rules.remediation: Declare providers in `standard.stream_flow.DependencyResolver` with explicit priority tiers, readiness probes, and fallback targets.

rules.name: Streaming Composition of Modules, Components & Processes
rules.statement: Cross-module, cross-component, and cross-process workflows MUST be composed as lazy, backpressure-aware generator streams (`StreamPipeline` of `StreamStage` nodes with kind `module | component | process`) ordered by prioritized topological sort (`depends_on` + lexicographic tier/weight), maintaining O(1) per-item memory and emitting a SHA-256 `StreamReceipt`.
rules.remediation: Compose multi-step workflows using `standard.stream_flow.StreamPipeline` and `StreamStage` instead of monolithic in-memory batch orchestrators.
